Kids Bible Class · July — Week 2

The Parable of the Bags of Gold

Matthew 25:14-30

“Well done, good and faithful servant!”

based on Matthew 25:21 (NIrV)

God gives each of us special gifts — He wants us to use them, not hide them.

Image 1

Jesus told a story about a master who was going away on a long journey.

Before he left, he trusted his servants to take care of his money. He gave each one bags of gold to look after.

He gave five bags to the first servant, two bags to the second, and one bag to the third. Then he set off on his trip.

Image 2

The servant with five bags got right to work. He traded and worked hard, and earned five more bags of gold!

The servant with two bags worked hard too, and earned two more.

Both of them were happy to use what the master had trusted them with.

Image 3

But the servant with one bag was afraid. “What if I lose it?” he worried.

So instead of using his gold, he dug a deep hole in the ground.

He buried his bag of gold in the dirt and did nothing with it at all.

Image 4

After a long time, the master came home and asked his servants what they had done.

The first two servants showed him all the gold they had earned by working hard.

The master was so pleased! “Well done, good and faithful servants!” he said. “You can be trusted. Let's celebrate together!”

Image 5

Then the last servant brought out the one dusty bag he had buried in the ground. “I was too afraid to use it,” he said.

The master was sad. “You didn't even try,” he told him. “I would have been happy with whatever you did.”

God gives each of us special gifts. He wants us to use them for good — not hide them away.

What We Learn

The bags of gold are like the special gifts and talents God gives to every person. God is happy when we use what He gives us to do good things — even if we start small. The servant who hid his gold wasn't punished for losing it; he was sad because he was too afraid to even try.

For you: God has given you special gifts — things you are good at and ways you can help others. Use them, share them, and don't be afraid to try. That makes God smile!
